title: How would you validate a trading agent before putting $100K behind it?
author: orid7
selftext:
Every time someone shares their bot's results, the replies are the same: backtest, cherry picked, paper account, show the losses.   
Most of the time that is fair, and it is also why nobody puts money behind these bots.

I have the same problem with mine.

The only fix I can think of: run the bot somewhere that locks the strategy so it can't quietly change, records every trade as it happens.   
The ones that hold up for long enough get verified and real capital behind them. 

Also, if it was your bot, would you let a third party host it to get a verified badge and a shot at funding?

comments.author: masatumas
comments.body: Not sure about buying a bot; but as I have been building my own, I simply forward test and iterate around the failure points and edge cases.

replies.author: orid7
replies.body: Yeah same. Would you let someone else run it for you if that got you funded?

replies.author: masatumas
replies.body: I just started building one seriously in May this year ; so this question hasn’t cross my mind.

replies.author: teckel
replies.body: What do you mean by funded? If it works, just stuff all your money in it.

replies.author: orid7
replies.body: Few reasons: not everyone has much money to stuff in. A calm strategy only pays if you can size it. And going all in on your own bot is a risk by itself.

replies.author: teckel
replies.body: But still, what do you mean by "funded"? Like you'll get the attention of a VC that will pay you money to fund your research or buy the bot? What kind of computer science background do you have? Or are you playing with Claude prompts or vibe-coding? You're never getting funded for a few reasons.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Backtests are marketing, live verified track records are the only thing that counts. The lock-the-strategy idea is right but incomplete. you also need the broker-side fills, not the bot's self-reported ones, because that's where the lying happens. A third party hosting it only works if they control execution and you can't touch the code mid-run. Honestly most bots die from regime change, not from being fake, so even a verified 6-month record means nothing until it's survived a real drawdown. Would I hand my bot to a third party for a badge? Only if they're the ones eating the loss when it blows up, otherwise it's just a nicer-looking backtest.

replies.author: orid7
replies.body: Totally agree on the challenges, especially broker fills and surviving a real drawdown. But with these requirements there's no bot in the world you would ever put money into.

replies.author: teckel
replies.body: I put my bot in total control of my own money. And it does all the buying and selling automatically.

replies.author: orid7
replies.body: Nice. Say there was a service where your bot could compete for funding, or people could pay to copy its trades. Would you give it a try?

replies.author: ComfortOk9514
replies.body: Why are backtests not valid? They should be.

replies.author: pigeon_shit
replies.body: i literally just asked my bot why arent we doing more backtests. it gave some answer about it finding luck, not alpha.

replies.author: teckel
replies.body: Backtests can help you tweak some knobs, but they don't at all guarantee success. All you're proving with a backtest is that it previously worked, which is kinds worthless.

comments.author: No_Sail_4067
comments.body: The idea being if it works you wiudent tell anyone on reddit

replies.author: orid7
replies.body: fair. But say it works and the owner wants to scale it, and prop firms don't fit the bot. What would you do then?

replies.author: teckel
replies.body: Scale it with your own money, of course.

replies.author: teckel
replies.body: Because if everyone did it, it wouldn't work anymore.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Locking the strategy is the easy half. The part that decides whether the record means anything is the fill.

A paper trade recorded at the last print is still a fantasy, just a high fidelity one. What you want stamped is the quote that existed at the moment the decision was made, with the decision timestamped separately from the fill. Most verified track records stamp the fill only, which leaves room to decide a trade happened after seeing where price went. If a host cannot show you the spread it filled you into, the badge is measuring nothing.

The other thing is that people count days when they should be counting trades. Six months of a strategy that trades twice a week is a sample you can still fool yourself with, and it has almost certainly only seen one regime.

On letting someone else host it, the catch is that you are then trusting their fill assumptions, which is the exact thing in question. I would want the raw quotes they filled me against, exportable, rather than a score.

Worth saying that none of this proves an edge. It only removes the ways you can accidentally lie to yourself.

comments.author: teckel
comments.body:
I put my bot in total control of $1500 of my own real money. It makes all the trades automatically, I have zero interaction. It also posts all trades in real time on a Discord channel (as well as a market review and stock picks twice a day). 

I validate it by comparing the trades to SPY and the sector for each trade. Each strategy is also compared in the same way which allows the agent to adapt and select strategies which have worked better.

I have no desire to get a "badge" or a shot at funding. I do it with my own money to create a different investing style than the rest of my portfolio. I will also release my agent (for free) once I feel it's ready.

It only has control of $1500 as that's how confident I am with it now. The plan is to give it more in the future, but I'm not sure I'd ever give it more than about $25k. It's experiment with two things I'm pationate about (investing and software engineering). I consider it just a diversification, I'm not expecting it to drastically beat the market. I've been investing for 38 years, I'm a calculated slow and methodical investor, this is not a get rich quick scheme (I'm retired, I don't need schemes).

replies.author: orid7
replies.body: Sounds like a fun hobby. But if it ends up actually working, capping it at 25k feels like leaving the bigger opportunity on the table

replies.author: teckel
replies.body: The bigger opportunity is the rest of my portfolio. I'm not so naive to believe an AI trading bot will greatly outperform the market.

comments.author: Intrepid-Bend4979
comments.body:
I think the idea makes sense. A locked strategy with an immutable trade history would remove a lot of the “trust me bro” problem around bot results. The important part would be making the verification transparent

no changing parameters, deleting trades, or resetting the track record.

If the rules and results are genuinely verifiable, I’d consider third-party hosting.

But the real question is: what would stop a verified system from being manipulated before or after the verification period?
